page: Amazon Web Services c6g.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance powered by a 64-core AWS Graviton2 processor built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation, the server eliminates hyperthreading overhead and virtualization contention. It includes 128 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core, along with a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local storage, relying exclusively on network-attached storage architectures, and does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core scaling alongside modest single-thread capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core compute tests such as stress-ng, Clang software compilation, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations. Furthermore, cached small-block memory reads demonstrate exceptional throughput. Conversely, single-core metrics—including Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and text processing—fall into the bottom quartiles, reflecting the moderate 2.5 GHz per-core clock rate and absence of x86 vector extensions like AVX-512.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton2 ARM platform delivers high core density and efficient multi-threaded compute per watt compared to legacy x86 equivalents. Workloads requiring extreme single-thread execution speed or heavy local scratch disks may find the lack of local NVMe and moderate single-core speeds limiting. However, the c6g.metal configuration is exceptionally suited for high-concurrency microservices, static web infrastructure, distributed Redis caching layers, and multi-threaded CI/CD compilation pipelines optimized for the ARM64 ecosystem.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server equipped with a 64-core ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processor running at 2.5 GHz with dedicated physical cores. It features 128 GB of DDR4 memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no integrated GPUs and provides no bundled local storage, requiring external block storage for persistent data. Performance data demonstrates strong multi-threaded execution, high cached memory bandwidth, and superior throughput in Redis caching and Clang software compilation benchmarks. However, single-core processing scores and LLM generation throughput are comparatively modest due to the 2.5 GHz clock ceiling and lack of AVX extensions. With high core density and bare-metal execution efficiency, c6g.metal is well suited for multi-threaded container workloads, web serving, distributed in-memory caching, and ARM-native software build clusters.
